US.description: Covers groceries, transportation, utilities, dining out, and miscellaneous expenses for a moderate urban lifestyle.

IN.description: Relatively low compared to Western countries, covering groceries, local transport, utilities, and dining out.

SG.description: Very high cost of living, particularly for transportation, imported goods, and dining out. Groceries are also on the higher side. Public transport is efficient.

CH.description: Cost of living is very high, particularly for groceries, public transportation, mandatory health insurance premiums, and dining out.

NL.description: Cost of living is relatively high, driven by groceries, transportation, and dining, but public transport is efficient. Utilities can also be significant.

GB.description: Covers groceries, utilities, transportation, and leisure for a single person.

CA.description: Cost of living, excluding rent, is moderately high across major Canadian cities, covering expenses like groceries, transportation, and utilities. The index reflects an average across various cities, with specific metropolitan areas like Toronto and Vancouver being higher.

AE.description: Cost of living, excluding rent, is high in major cities, especially for dining, entertainment, and imported goods. Groceries can be moderate.

NO.description: Significantly high costs for groceries, transportation, and leisure activities due to high wages and taxes.

IE.description: Cost of living, excluding rent, covers groceries, transportation, utilities, and leisure activities, with Dublin being notably higher than other Irish regions.

LU.description: High costs for groceries, transportation, utilities, and dining out, reflecting Luxembourg's status as an expensive country.

AU.description: Cost of living, excluding rent, is generally high across Australia, with groceries, dining out, and utilities being notably expensive.

QA.description: High overall cost of living, particularly for housing and imported goods, but personal income is tax-free.

BN.description: Cost of living is moderate, generally lower than Western countries but higher than some neighboring Southeast Asian nations, especially for imported goods and services.

MO.description: High cost of imported goods, groceries, and dining out, balanced by relatively low public transport fares.
